newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Macau, HK workers demonstrate in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Macau, HK workers demonstrate in Taiwan.

text.p: Hong Kong and Macau citizens living in Taiwan demonstrated in the capital Taipei on Thursday to demand the right to continue working freely on the island after their homelands revert to Chinese rule.

Chanting "free working rights" and "we are supporters of the Republic of China," some 100 residents from Hong Kong and Macau demonstrated outside the cabinet's Labour Affairs Council to demand the council drop a plan to restrict their work rights.
"We have declared our loyalty to the Republic of China (Taiwan) government, and it would be unfair if it restricted our rights to work in Taiwan," activist Chou Ching-chun told Reuters by telephone.

On April 15, the council approved a plan to require Hong Kong and Macau citizens to obtain permits to work in Taiwan after the hanover of the British and Portugese enclaves to China in July 1997 and December 1999.
Residents from the two territories currently are treated the same as Taiwan nationals and do not need work permits.

"If the planned measure was targeted at pro-Chinese communist Hong Kong or Macau people, we would not say anything, but for people who support the ROC it would be unfair," said Chou, chairman of Hong Kong and Macau Residents Association.
He said they had long registered with Taiwan authorities as "overseas Chinese" -- people who support Taiwan -- and could face political persecution by Beijing after the handover.
"We would not rule out more radical actions if our free working rights were rejected," said Chou.

A council spokesman told Retuers the new requirement was in line with the government's Hong Kong-Macau Relations act, passed by parliament on March 18 to govern Taiwan's trade and other activities with the two territories after the Chinese takeover.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese soverignty on July 1, 1997 after more than 150 years of British rule. Macau will be handed back to Beijing on December 20, 1999, ending Portuguese control since 1557.
Taiwan -- China's bitter rival since a civil war split them in 1949 -- would then treat the two territories as special administrative areas and maintain its current operations there.
Hong Kong and Macau citizens would be treated as foreigners, and unless they register as "overseas Chinese" they would not be able to work in Taiwan, council officials said.

They said an "overseas Chinese" from either Hong Kong or Macau would be allowed to work indefinitely in Taiwan after obtaining an employment letter and registering with the labour council, unlike other foreigners.
Taiwan work permits are good for two years and then must be renewed. Foreigners must also pass physical examinations, including blood test.
Hong Kong has about 6.4 million people and Macau about 450,000. About 50,000 to 60,000 people from the two territories currently work in Taiwan.
